questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I heard lots of great things about studying in Melbourne.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: At information meetings on campus at University of Melbourne they told us about where to find information in both the University website and at Stop1.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember getting any assistance from the university. But if you wish the university offers to pick exchange students up from the airport and transport them to their accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to know someone from back home that had lived in Melbourne for a year and was going back home at the same time is was coming to Melbourne. So we did a lease transfer and I took over their apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rent is similar to Copenhagen prices depending on where you find accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When I arrived they had a information meeting where I received information on how to register. I stopped by stop1 to get the student Id that I ordered online from the myunimelb website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the help you needed could be obtained from Stop1. They give you the option to book a time slot online or simply show up. They will help you with almost everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost 100% succesful. There was only 1 subject where the professor didn't reply to my request to join his subject.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I remember things to be pretty straight forward but if you have questions Stop1 will help with almost everything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 1 year subjects on the BA programme, which were all very good for 1 year students. I think 3 year subjects would have been a better suit for the knowledge I have already gathered from my 2 years of studying at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of assignments that are due every couple of weeks. On my BA of biology at UCPH I don't often have assignments throughout my semester. Besides the exams at UCPH usually accounts for 100% of the final grade while exams at UniMelb only accounts for about 50% and assignments throughout the semester make up the other percentage of the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Insects Shaping Society
Australian Flora and Fauna

Plant Biodiversity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: That depends on which BA you are enrolled in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gym clubs, mountaineering clubs, K-pop clubs almost everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club to meet locals and other exchange students. Or if you do sports then joining a sports team to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the National Parks in the state, go to weekend markets around the city e.g. Fitzroy markets, walk around the city and explore nice cafees etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy Melbourne is very similar in to Copenhagen in terms of the vibe of the city. People are very friendly in stores, cafees and everywhere you go. Always interested in talking to you and making new friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Show up for on campus lectures and practical classes. People in Melbourne are very social and most are interested in making new friends and talking to you

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found no big challenges in any cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are so friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do yourself a favor and properly research which subjects are available to you before you leave Copenhagen. I could have had more interesting subjects if I had spent more time looking in to what was available to me. 

Show up to on campus lectures and practical classes to meet potential friends and people that might have similar interests to you. 

Explore and make good use of the very large campus that University of Melbourne has.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to ask teachers for help, most of them are very kind and will gladly help you with questions regarding their subjects.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in the awesome city Melbourne that homes so many different ethnicities and types of people. People are so friendly

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time management - figuring out how to spend time on school, friends, hobbies and exploring the country while on exchange. You will probably find it hard to make time for everything

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
